A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SEEA-R1 and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained material can be matched across renumbering and relocation, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original ALFWorld experiments, EmbodiedEval evaluations, multimodal benchmark results, and appendix ablations and trajectory analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds physical-robot evaluations, reward-model accuracy measurements, reasoning-trace comparisons, and computational-cost results.

M1.justification: Section 3.2.2 replaces v1's generic GRPO-based reward-model training description with GT-supervised cross-entropy training and periodic calibration, plus a GT-free TTRL/GRPO procedure using majority-voted pseudo-labels. v2 also introduces probabilistic MCTS expansion and a path budget. These change the specified training and search procedures; the Tree-GRPO policy objective remains unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds physical-robot evaluation across six household environments, with 12 tasks per environment, extending coverage beyond simulated environments and generated-video exploration. ALFWorld, EmbodiedEval, and the general multimodal benchmarks already evaluated in v1 are retained.

E2.justification: EmbodiedEval Table 3 adds Vision-R1-7B and Ocean-R1, reporting overall scores of 8.54 and 15.85. Appendix D.1 also introduces a reported PPO training-time comparison. Existing ALFWorld and EmbodiedEval comparators remain, including those in v1 Table 2, relocated to v2 Table 7.

E3.justification: Section 4.1.2 changes the reported MGRM GRPO group size from 24 to 10 and the KL coefficient from 0.01 to 0.0. New physical experiments specify front-camera observations and human-teleoperated, single-trajectory execution over 72 cases. These are substantive setting changes and an additional evaluation protocol; the ALFWorld splits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 expands the reward ablation into supervised and self-supervised comparisons and adds reward-state accuracy diagnostics, training/inference efficiency analyses, and reasoning-trace comparisons between the baseline and successive training iterations. The sample-size, long-training, and generated-data analyses in v1 Appendix H are retained in v2 Appendix G.

E5.justification: v1 Figure 5 displays vertical error bars on the reward-comparison curves; its replacement, v2 Figure 6, omits them. Other retained plots preserve their error bars or shaded bands. Neither version explains these uncertainty displays or supplies corresponding seed or repeated-run counts.

E6.justification: Reported multimodal ALFWorld success changes from 36.19% to 46.27% with GT rewards and from 23.88% to 44.03% without GT rewards. Training and reward procedures also change, so these are revised system results rather than controlled same-setting gains. v2 adds real-world results of 68.1% versus the baseline's 33.3%, reward-accuracy measurements, and cost results. Existing text-only ALFWorld and SEEA-R1's 19.88% EmbodiedEval results remain.

T1.justification: v2 adds asymptotic complexity assertions for pruned MCTS in Section 4.2.4 and Appendix D.1. The POMDP formulation, Tree-GRPO objective, and MCTS equations are retained. No supporting theorem or proof accompanies the new complexity assertions.

C1.justification: The main claims remain the first RFT framework for self-evolving embodied agents, the Tree-GRPO and MGRM contributions, ALFWorld state-of-the-art performance, and learning without environmental GT rewards. v2 updates headline results and emphasizes policy–reward co-refinement already described in v1, without materially redefining these central claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of physical-world transfer through learned reflection and correction, explains frozen-MGRM failures through premature termination caused by Continue-to-Failure misclassification, and discusses the computational cost of avoiding GT supervision. These substantially extend the mechanism and applicability discussion. The original limitation concerning unpredictable real-world environments is merely moved to Appendix M.

D1.justification: v2 adds the robot platform and execution details, the complete real-world task inventory and prompt, vLLM inference information, reward-training and pruning parameters, and stage-specific timing measurements. These materially expand reproducibility documentation. The project-page address changes, while the promise to open-source the framework remains.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion of Wang et al.'s embodied planner and AlphaLLM-CPL, alongside citations supporting TTRL, physical experiments, Ocean-R1, and vLLM. It removes v1's localized claims of first extending this approach to physically grounded vision-language tasks and previously unexplored MCTS-based embodied training. Most related-work discussion remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Editing is concentrated in reward-model training, reward ablations, and related work, with added experimental subsections and appendix sections. The limitations paragraph moves to the appendix, appendix headings are reorganized, and author/header text changes. Much of the original narrative remains verbatim; the scientific additions do not constitute a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds a physical-execution figure, reasoning-trace boxes, and tables for real-world performance, inference efficiency, reward accuracy, task inventories, and training costs. The reward-ablation figure becomes a redesigned two-panel display. Several existing appendix plots are enlarged, and the text-only ALFWorld table moves to the appendix; those retained displays are not new evidence.

improvement.justification: Physical-task validation and more explicit reward-training and implementation descriptions improve empirical grounding and reproducibility beyond v1. However, the added analyses contain unresolved reporting problems: Table 8's overall counts do not reconcile with its class counts, and Appendix L.3's 248-minute total conflicts with Table 10's 421.5 minutes. Together with removed reward-ablation error bars, these weaknesses limit the net quality gain.
